description:
Split out of op-ja3t so the solver capability is tracked separately from the Marviken test that motivated it. Written during the session that died at ~12:52 on 2026-08-11.

WHERE: crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/drift_flux.rs, +476 lines, WORKING TREE ONLY, not committed, not backed up anywhere.

WHAT IT ADDS (read off the diff, not from a design doc):
- InflowState and BoundaryFaceState — a boundary-face state machine replacing the previous fixed inlet handling.
- resolve_boundary(), left_pressure_face_predictor(), right_pressure_face_predictor().
- upwind_scalar(field, flux, upstream, downstream) — donor-cell face value.
- A plenum stagnation inflow condition parameterised by stagnation pressure p_0 [Pa] and stagnation specific enthalpy h_0 [J/kg], documented as assuming (a) drift velocity is zero at the inlet, since a stagnant plenum has no relative phase motion, and (b) the plenum is infinite and does not deplete.

STATE: `cargo check -p tampines --lib --tests` passes. `cargo test --release -p tampines --lib multiphase_1d` -> 6 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored, 44.24 s — but NONE of those 6 exercises the new boundary condition. The only consumer is the unfinished Marviken harness in marviken_tests.rs (op-ja3t), whose gate tests were never written. So this code is UNVERIFIED, not merely un-validated: no test has ever run through the new inflow path.

WHAT REMAINS:
1. Decide whether to land it as-is or hold it until op-ja3t exercises it. It is currently the only thing keeping the tampines tree dirty.
2. Write at least one direct unit test of the stagnation inflow — e.g. that a zero-velocity initial field driven by a plenum at p_0 accelerates to the incompressible Bernoulli limit for a single-phase subcooled inlet, which has a closed-form answer independent of the Marviken data.
3. Document methodology AND measured results per the workspace V&V rule once it is exercised.
4. State the two assumptions above in the public doc comment of whatever type users construct, not only at the call site.

Blocks: op-ja3t (the Marviken drift-flux gate cannot run without a stagnation inflow).

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
Stagnation inflow BC now EXERCISED AND VERIFIED for the single-phase subcooled steady path, 2026-08-11 (~17:00 SGT). Items 2, 3, 4 of this bead are done; item 1 (land vs hold) stays a maintainer decision.

NEW TEST: reservoir_inlet_reaches_the_bernoulli_limit_in_subcooled_water in crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/tests.rs (+~390 lines incl. V&V doc). Closed form derived from the DISCRETE steady state of the scheme's own momentum balances (not the continuum limit): p0 - p_out = rho u^2/2 + rho F L with Darcy F, giving u = sqrt(2 dp / (rho (1 + f L/D))), friction incorporated (not neglected) via the code's own laminar-64/Re / Blasius closure. Case: p0 1.000 MPa -> p_out 0.980 MPa, T 300 K (~153 K subcooled), L 0.5 m, D 0.1 m, 20 cells, dt 0.5 ms, 3000 steps; all solver knobs at defaults.

MEASURED: closed-form u 6.225884 m/s vs measured steady inlet u 6.225891 m/s -> relative error +1.12e-6 against a 1.0 % tolerance PRE-COMMITTED in the doc comment before the first run (a-priori budget ~0.1 %, gated 10x looser because reference f is evaluated once at (p_out, mu_f)). Frictionless Bernoulli would be 6.334222 m/s; measured sits 1.7102 % below, matching the friction correction. Continuity |mdot_in - mdot_out|/mdot 1.28e-6; steadiness 3.3e-7; max Courant 0.125; alpha = 0 exactly throughout; ~6-7 s wall clock. Strongest evidence: the three pressure terms match INDIVIDUALLY (p[0] 980661.291 predicted vs 980661.29 measured; interior drop 644.376 vs 644.33; outflow face 16.957 vs 16.96), separately confirming the conservative half-cell inlet convection, the half-cell Dirichlet coefficient dt/(rho dx/2), and friction charged over exactly L. No defect found; the non-conservative alternative the BC doc warns about would sit at ~4.48 m/s (-28 %) and nothing near that appears.

DOCS: AxialBoundary::ReservoirInlet public doc now states both standing assumptions (zero inlet drift velocity; infinite non-depleting plenum) plus a V&V status block — doc-comment-only edits to drift_flux.rs, no code/signature/constant changed.

ALSO EXERCISED INDIRECTLY: the Marviken gates (op-ja3t) drive this BC through 897 marched two-phase transients with 0 refused steps.

STILL UNVERIFIED (stated in the test doc and the ReservoirInlet V&V block): two-phase inflow (InflowState::void_fraction and rho_g never exercised, alpha = 0 throughout the direct test), the h0 - u^2/2 static-enthalpy split only probed at 2e-4 relative head, backflow through either boundary, and transient behaviour. upwind_scalar has no direct unit test — it is private to drift_flux and tests.rs is a sibling module, so it needs a pub(super) visibility change first; filed as a follow-up bead (see op tracker, filed today). Note also Blasius is applied at Re ~ 4.1e6, beyond its nominal ~1e5 range — a property of the code under test, reproduced not corrected. Not closing this bead — maintainer decision.

title: tampines: drift-flux plenum stagnation inflow BC — written 2026-08-11, uncommitted and unexercised
